review_flags: 'up_to' rendered as 'تک', which in Urdu is a postposition and normally follows the number (e.g. '$10 تک'). If the UI concatenates it BEFORE a figure (English word order), the phrasing will read awkwardly — verify how the template composes 'up to' + amount.
'per_lot' kept as '/ لاٹ' with a leading slash inside RTL text — confirm the slash renders on the correct side when appended to a number.
Tier names Bronze/Prime transliterated as 'برانز'/'پرائم'. Confirm these match TNFX's official tier naming (they may prefer English tier labels).

Frequent Latin-script loanwords (forex, per lot, withdraw, referral, affiliate, CFD, instruments, FX) embedded in RTL Urdu — check bidirectional rendering, especially where a loanword sits next to Urdu punctuation or the '#1' / '$' figures.
Regulatory disclaimer (footer_disclaimer) financial phrasing localized — have a compliance reviewer confirm the Urdu risk-warning wording is acceptable for a regulated broker.
'challenge/quests/missions' gaming metaphor rendered as 'چیلنج ارینا / کویسٹس / مشنز' (transliterations). Confirm this energetic marketing tone is desired vs. more formal Urdu equivalents.
Meta descriptions were kept concise but Urdu is more verbose than English; double-check each stays near the ~150-char target and isn't truncated in SERPs.
